title: Grieving with others
hook: stay present when you don't know what to say
tomorrow: why did Peter refuse to let Jesus wash his feet?

segments.voice: Yesterday, a garden at night and three friends asleep: Jesus knew loneliness too. The line was not alone in it. Today, someone else's grief.

Bad news lands in the group chat: so sorry, a heart, then silence. When you don't know what to say, staying away can start to feel polite. Maybe they want space. Maybe you'd only make it worse. In John's Gospel, Jesus reaches Bethany four days after his friend Lazarus has died. He already knows what he'll do; he's told his disciples he is going to wake him. Then Mary, Lazarus's sister, falls at his feet weeping, and the people who came to comfort her are weeping too. And Jesus…
screen: `SO SORRY. THEN SILENCE.` → `FOUR DAYS IN THE TOMB.` → `MARY AT HIS FEET.`

segments.voice: "And Jesus wept." Three words in the Douay-Rheims, and they answer the puzzle. He isn't crying because he's lost hope; soon he'll call Lazarus out of the tomb. John says that when he saw Mary weeping, and those with her weeping, he groaned in spirit and was troubled. He wept because they were weeping. He didn't open with the plan or explain anything to a sister on the floor. He stood in the grief with them first, and the people watching said, behold how he loved him. Paul makes it a habit in his letter to the Romans: "weep with them that weep." Not fix it, not explain it: weep with. Its twin sits in the same verse, rejoice with them that rejoice: the same presence, in joy and in sorrow. Even the neighbors in this story know it. John says people had come from Jerusalem to comfort the sisters, and their coming was the comfort. Catholics build this into the way they bury their dead. Before the funeral there can be a vigil, where the community gathers with the family to pray and keep them company. So when you don't know what to say, the story's answer is that you may not need to. Bring yourself. Then stay.
screen: `AND JESUS WEPT.` · `HE WEPT BECAUSE THEY WEPT.` · `WEEP WITH THEM THAT WEEP.` · `A VIGIL BEFORE THE FUNERAL.` · then, large: `JUST STAY.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and bring to mind someone who is grieving right now, close to you or not. Don't plan what to say to them. Just sit beside them in your mind for the whole stretch, the way you'd sit in a quiet room with nothing to fix. If you pray, you can hold their name before God; if not, simply hold it with care.
Grieving with others. Standing inside someone's sorrow with them, before any explanation, and sometimes without one. Today's word.
Keep this one: just stay, the way Jesus stood weeping before he said a word. Till tomorrow, then.

chat.says: mia's grandma died. i'm going to the shiva tonight. what do i even say? i'm so bad at this
options: Maybe not much. Jesus wept with Mary before he said anything. Go, sit near Mia, and stay.
Have a good line ready about her grandma being in a better place, so Mia has hope.
Text instead. A shiva is for family, and it's easier for Mia with no visitors.
chat.meaning: Jesus wept with the mourners before he said a word, and Paul says weep with them that weep. Presence is the comfort; words can wait.

Lazarus.meaning: Jesus's friend in Bethany, brother of Martha and Mary

Bethany.meaning: a village near Jerusalem where Lazarus lived

vigil.meaning: a prayer gathering with the family before a funeral

Douay-Rheims.meaning: an older English Catholic translation of the Bible

sources.ref: Order of Christian Funerals: Vigil for the Deceased

notes: John 11:35 ('And Jesus wept.') and Romans 12:15 ('weep with them that weep') quoted from Douay-Rheims; confirm. 'Three words in the Douay-Rheims' counts 'And Jesus wept'.

John 11:33 ('groaned in the spirit, and troubled himself'), 11:36 ('Behold how he loved him') and 11:19 (people came from Jerusalem to comfort the sisters) paraphrased. The text's 'the Jews' is rendered 'the people who came to comfort her' / 'people from Jerusalem' to avoid a careless framing; confirm.
Trapdoor: John 11:33 uses klaiō for Mary's and the mourners' weeping, 11:35 dakryō for Jesus. Confirm.
Vigil for the Deceased (Order of Christian Funerals) described simply; confirm.
